newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call eases as focus turns to bond auction.
newsitem.headline: Indian call eases as focus turns to bond auction.

text.p: Indian call money closed lower at 1.50-2.00 percent on Tuesday against the day's opening levels of 2.50-3.50 percent, dealers said.
Most of the deals were at 2.25-2.75 percent, while some stray deals were struck at 1.50-1.75 percent levels, they said.
The call rates are expected to open above 3.50 percent levels on Wednesday on expected outflows, a dealer said.
The market expects a 20 billion rupee later on Tuesday to be fully subscribed. Tax outflows are also expected to affect liquidity, dealers said.
The next fortnight may see some tightness in the call levels, ICICI securities and Finance Company said.
It estimated total outflows at 54.5 billion rupees and inflows at 38.33 billion rupees.
The securities market was dull and lacklusture on Tuesday, dealers said. Bankers were waiting results of the seven-year bond auction results before initiating any fresh positions.
The volume on trade on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) was 1.8 billion rupees compared to previous 1.17 billion rupees, a NSE dealer said.
The 12.69 percent government stock 2002 fell to 101.32 rupees against its previous close of 101.35 rupees, while the 12.14 percent 2000 was steady at 100.69 rupees, he said.
